rules.decision: Classify a study as randomized experimental only when the investigator assigns the intervention or exposure using a random allocation mechanism.
rules.action: Set randomized=true, preserve treatment assignment and analysis-set information, and route causal interpretation through the randomized design rather than an observational-association workflow.
assumptions: Random allocation was implemented as described
warnings: Random sampling from a population is not the same as random assignment to treatment.
Do not discard randomized participants or redefine analysis groups without an explicit analysis-set rule and justification.
exceptions: Cluster-randomized trials also require cluster-aware analysis.

source_evidence.support: Penn State distinguishes experimental from observational studies and uses random assignment as the randomized-experiment feature.
ICH E9 emphasizes preservation of randomization and analysis sets close to the intention-to-treat ideal.

rules.decision: Do not analyze an interrupted time series as a simple before-versus-after comparison.
conditions: Outcome is measured repeatedly over ordered time points
A defined intervention, policy, or interruption occurs at a known time
rules.action: Represent pre-interruption trend, interruption timing, post-interruption level and slope, and serial dependence explicitly. Consider level change, slope change, or both according to the research question.
diagnostics: Number and spacing of pre/post observations
Seasonality or other time-patterns where relevant
warnings: A pre/post mean comparison can confound an intervention effect with an existing trend.
Ignoring autocorrelation can invalidate ordinary regression standard errors.
exceptions: Individual repeated-measures data are not automatically an interrupted time series; subject-level correlation may require longitudinal models.

source_evidence.support: The source defines ITS as before/after time-series analysis, warns against simple pre/post comparison, requires attention to pre-interruption trend and autocorrelation, and distinguishes level and slope changes.
source_evidence.section: What is ITS Analysis? / Time Series Caveats / ITS Analysis

rules.decision: Classify and preserve the actual probability-sampling design rather than defaulting to simple random sampling.
conditions: A sample rather than complete enumeration is used
Selection probabilities are known or generated by a probability-based design
rules.action: Record the design as simple random, systematic, stratified, cluster, multistage, PPS, or a documented combination; retain selection probabilities, weights, strata, clusters/PSUs, and stages needed for analysis.
assumptions: Sampling documentation reflects the implemented design
warnings: Do not convert a complex probability design to an iid simple-random-sample analysis by dropping its design variables.
Probability sampling and random treatment assignment are different concepts.
exceptions: A truly self-weighting design can have equal weights, but the design should still be declared.

source_evidence.support: UN guidance covers SRS, systematic, stratified, cluster and multistage probability designs and emphasizes probability sampling at each stage.
Penn State distinguishes probability-based SRS/stratified/cluster sampling from non-probability convenience sampling.

rules.decision: Do not treat convenience or other non-probability samples as probability samples with design-based population representativeness.
conditions: Sampling is convenience, volunteer/self-selected, purposive, or otherwise lacks known probability selection
rules.action: Record sampling as non-probability, preserve the stated recruitment mechanism, and flag population-generalization claims for substantive review rather than fabricating survey weights or sampling probabilities.
warnings: A large convenience sample does not become a probability sample because of sample size.
Do not invent selection probabilities or design weights when they are not known.
exceptions: Model-based generalization may be attempted under additional assumptions, but it is distinct from design-based probability-survey inference.

source_evidence.support: Penn State identifies convenience sampling as non-probability based and describes sampling bias when selection does not represent the target population.

rules.decision: Recognize census or complete enumeration as distinct from sampling and do not manufacture sampling-design variables for units that were not sampled.
conditions: All units in the defined target frame/population are intended to be enumerated
rules.action: Set sampling_mode=complete_enumeration and document coverage, nonresponse and measurement issues separately from sampling error.
assumptions: The stated frame defines the intended enumerated population
warnings: Complete enumeration removes sampling selection from the design but does not eliminate nonresponse, coverage, measurement, or processing error.
Do not automatically generalize beyond the enumerated target population.

source_evidence.support: UN guidance distinguishes censuses/complete enumeration from sample surveys and notes sampling is used when complete enumeration is impractical.
